top_signal.title: Been soft destroyed my business
top_signal.summary: Spent four years building my painting business. Now I’m owed $460k and trying to figure out how to rebuild.    I run a painting business in Melbourne, and honestly, this is a difficult post to write.   For four years, I worked practically every day. No family holiday during that time, and the only proper break I took was five days for my son’s birthday. I thought putting in those hours would eventually give my family some security.   A lot of my work came through builders who were family friends or friends of my dad. I trusted those relationships, and I’m now owed around $460,000 for work we’ve done.   I’ve stopped working with them, but walking away also meant losing a major source of work. Now I have an experienced painting crew and the ability to take on jobs, but I’m struggling to get enough work through the door.   The hardest part is thinking about how much time I spent working instead of being with my family, only to find myself in this position anyway.   I know I should have built a wider customer base and put firmer boundaries around those business relationships. I can see that clearly now. What I’m struggling with is how to move forward from here.   We do residential and commercial painting across Melbourne, from home repaints to medical and dental fit-outs. I’ve been contacting builders, following up old contacts and trying to find new leads, but I haven’t managed to build a steady flow of work.
